## Simple explanation

NumPy is a foundational Python library for working with arrays of numbers.
It makes common operations on vectors, matrices, and higher-dimensional
arrays concise and efficient.

## Technical explanation

Its core `ndarray` type stores homogeneous data in a multidimensional,
strided array. NumPy provides vectorized elementwise operations,
broadcasting, linear algebra routines, random-number generation, and
interfaces used by much of the scientific Python ecosystem.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Numerical data preparation, feature processing, and experimentation often
use NumPy arrays. Understanding array shapes, dtypes, and broadcasting
helps prevent subtle bugs and supports interoperability with libraries
such as pandas, scikit-learn, and PyTorch.

## How it works

Many operations are implemented in compiled code and applied to whole
arrays rather than through Python-level loops. Broadcasting allows
compatible shapes to participate in an operation without explicitly
copying a value across every element.

## Practical example

Given an array of feature values, subtracting its mean and dividing by its
standard deviation can standardize all values with concise array
operations. Always inspect shapes and handle zero-variance features
appropriately.

## Common misconceptions

- NumPy arrays are not interchangeable with every framework's tensor type; conversion and device placement may matter.
- Broadcasting can produce a mathematically unintended shape even when code runs successfully.
- Vectorization improves many numerical workloads but does not make every operation automatically faster or memory-free.
